newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber market sputters to weak close.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber market sputters to weak close.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market closed weakly on Friday, bedevilled by weak consumer demand as market players decided to take an early weekend break, dealers said.
Chinese buyers which made some inquiries earlier on Friday decided to stay out. With no major offtake seen, market activity sputtered as a result, traders said.
"There was almost no soul in the market today. Even the overseas buyers were not there," a dealer said.
"The overseas buyers have decided to take it easy. There are almost no orders in the market," another trader said.
Another dealer said the Chinese merely wanted an indication of prices and "were not really serious about buying."
Bridgestone, which asked for offers for SIR20 rubber earlier in the week, was not seen anymore, the dealers said.
Traders were apprehensive going into next week that prices will be squeezed down some more due to the end of wintering in most rubber-producing countries.
At around 0945 GMT, May RSS3 was seen at 116.50-117.50 U.S. cents a kg from 117.50 cents. July RSS1 was seen at 171.00-173.00 Singapore cents (US$1.19-$1.21) a kg from 172.00 cents.
